essence: No block for folk or devotees (1); the self seen at once despite ladders (2); laughing victors and vanquished (3); no dryness, no release-seeking (4); as unknown before, may it grow (5); the single prayer (6); drunk, angry, leaping, shouting Śiva (7); crisis or peace, tears or laughter — by devotion (8); nothing to be known, inside or out (9); rejoicing even at abusers (10); pain ripening to enjoyment (11); held everywhere, same touch-joy (12); duality's double-refuge dissolved (13); pilgrim-eyes err, Being shines (14); ripened mind unmannered (15); knowledge-rich put to shame (16); devotion-nectar-drink-and-bath as rite (17); world-life praiseworthy (18); liberation renamed as ripe devotion (19); pain invited, pleasure refused (20); mutual dependence blessed, not solved (21); form or formless, always nectar (22); another world-stand in this world (23); devotion, devotion, something (24); I weep, let fierce devotion be mine (25); jewel or straw, stuck to You priceless (26); unparted, they win (27); embraced in saṃsāra's hall (28); hugging Śiva with the feasting Goddess (29); sovereignty with no subjects, otherness by which the world shines as it does not (30).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of bursting (udbheda); the vyabhicāri is courage (dhairya) that nothing stands between devotee and Him. The rasa is the heroism of bursting bonds — no people, no gods, no method-ladders, no impurity, no sorrow, no logic stands between. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as vīra: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute unblocked. Lakshmanjoo: pāśānudbheda — bursting of the noose from inside, not cut from outside. Mutual dependence (anyonyāśraya, v.21) is blessed, not solved — the collection's frankest circle. Devotion is the only wealth that bursts all bonds.
